Use `Public|NonPublic` and check method flags with dnfile. - **Tame animals CAN open the player's doors** (`PawnKindDef.canOpenDoors` defaults true). What shuts wild animals, hostiles and prisoners out is the faction rule `GenAI.MachinesLike` inside `Building_Door.PawnCanOpen`, and a FACTIONLESS door (`jawa/spawn_batch` leaves doors factionless) lets a wild animal through. Model 'animal vs door' as 'cannot open the player's doors', not `!CanOpenDoors`. - **`Verse.Mod.GetSettings()` tracks ONE `ModSettings` per `Mod` object** (a private field, not keyed by type): a second call for a different `T` logs a `Log.Error` and returns null, with no exception. A constructor calling it for several types silently breaks the others (NRE in `DoSettingsWindowContents`, fields never persist). Make extra settings classes plain `new` and scribe them from the one real `ModSettings.ExposeData()`. - **A refusal added to a BUILT hook needs its mirror in the LOST hook,** and a settings toggle gating one path into a side effect must gate every other caller of it. Promote def floats to double before multiplying them into a time. A NextChange test with only lit 1 / short gaps cannot see this. - **A static (session-wide) table or cache keyed by thing/pawn ID breaks across fixture and save reloads:** a reload restarts BOTH the thing-ID counter and the tick, so the next session's first-spawned pawn inherits an old 'already handled' entry at a fresh-looking tick, and a 'too far ahead = stale' guard does not catch it. Put the arrival action in the job's own last toil. - **When you make a work method incremental, keep the public no-arg entry point's old complete contract;** slice only in the per-frame caller. A budgeted `Rebuild()` left scripted callers reading half-laid pieces; the fix was `Rebuild()` => `Rebuild(true)` with only frame paths calling `Rebuild(false)` (pinned by `selftest_gimmesomeslack.py sliced_rebuild_callers`). - **A versioned snapshot accessor called with `maxAge 0` on a hot path rebuilds the whole artifact every tick** even when its version proves nothing changed (per-lay `World()` did ~100 whole-map `CordWorld` rebuilds, ~0.85 MB each, in a 300-tick wave and forced full GCs).         {

        private static int SpecTier(float b, float t1, float t2, float t3, int force)
        {

                    }
                    // ruled footprints: T1 2x2, T2 3x3, T3 4x4 (Large Pawns' hard ceiling); an untiered size never reaches Large Pawns
                    Check(RM_TitanicKernel.FootprintSize(1) == 2 && RM_TitanicKernel.FootprintSize(2) == 3 && RM_TitanicKernel.FootprintSize(3) == 4, "footprints are not 2/3/4");
                    // TITAN_WAKE_FIXES_1 (B3.18 / C3.4): base and life-stage factor fuzzed independently. Any pawn whose CURRENT size
                    // (base x a stage factor no larger than the race's max) is tiered must belong to a race that qualifies for the comp.
                    for (int k = 0; k < 16; k++)
                    {
                        float bse = F(r, 0.1f, t3 * 1.2f), maxF = r.Next(4) == 0 ? F(r, 0.1f, 1f) : F(r, 1f, 4f);
                        float stage = F(r, 0.05f, Math.Max(maxF, 1f));
                        if (stage > maxF && maxF >= 1f) stage = maxF;
                        if (maxF < 1f) stage = Math.Min(stage, 1f);
                        int now = RM_TitanicKernel.TierFor(bse * stage, t1, t2, t3, 0);
                        bool qual = RM_TitanicKernel.DefQualifies(bse, maxF, t1, 0);
                        Check(!(now != 0 && !qual), $"life stage x{stage} (max {maxF}) on base {bse} is tier {now} but the race does not qualify for the wake comp");
                        Check(qual == (bse * Math.Max(maxF, 1f) >= t1), "DefQualifies(base, factor) is not base x max(factor, 1) >= T1");
                        Check(RM_TitanicKernel.DefQualifies(bse, maxF, t1, -1) == false && RM_TitanicKernel.DefQualifies(bse, maxF, t1, 1), "force ignored with a life-stage factor");
                    }
                    // HUGETHINGS_SETTINGS_HARDENING_1 (B3.19 / C3.6 / D3.3): hostile Scribe values (NaN, +-inf, negative, zero, huge) end sane.
                    Check(!RM_TitanicKernel.ThresholdsValid(t1, t2, float.PositiveInfinity) && !RM_TitanicKernel.ThresholdsValid(float.NaN, t2, t3)
                          && !RM_TitanicKernel.ThresholdsValid(t1, float.PositiveInfinity, float.PositiveInfinity), "ThresholdsValid accepts an infinite or NaN rung");
                    foreach (float bad in new[] { float.NaN, float.PositiveInfinity, float.NegativeInfinity, -F(r, 0f, 1e6f), 0f, F(r, 0f, 1e9f) })
                    {
                        float lo = F(r, 0f, 5f), hi = lo + F(r, 0.01f, 50f), dflt = F(r, lo, hi);
                        float got = RM_TitanicKernel.SaneSetting(bad, lo, hi, dflt);
                        Check(RM_TitanicKernel.Finite(got) && got >= lo && got <= hi, $"SaneSetting({bad}) = {got} outside [{lo},{hi}]");
                        if (!RM_TitanicKernel.Finite(bad)) Check(got == dflt, $"non-finite {bad} did not fall back to the default");
                        Check(RM_TitanicKernel.Finite(RM_TitanicKernel.SaneSetting(bad, lo, hi, float.NaN)), "a NaN default escaped");
                        int ib = float.IsNaN(bad) ? 0 : (int)Math.Max(int.MinValue / 2, Math.Min(int.MaxValue / 2, bad));
                        int ig = RM_TitanicKernel.SaneSetting(ib, 1, 50);
                        Check(ig >= 1 && ig <= 50, $"int SaneSetting({ib}) = {ig}");
                    }
                }
                catch (Exception e) { fails.Add($"tier seed {seed}: {e.Message}"); }
            }
            return fails;
        }

        private static List<string> Yield(int cases, int seed0)
        {
            var fails = new List<string>();
            for (int c = 0; c < cases; c++)
            {
                int seed = seed0 + c; var r = new Random(seed); Cases++;
                try
                {
                    float t1, t2, t3; Ladder(r, out t1, out t2, out t3);
                    float minF = F(r, 0.05f, 1f);
                    foreach (int tier in new[] { 1, 2 })
                    {
                        float floor = RM_TitanicKernel.YieldFloor(tier, t1, t2);
                        Check(floor == (tier == 1 ? t1 : t2), "YieldFloor wrong");
                        float prevF = 2f, prevTotal = 0f, prevB = 0f;
                        for (int i = 0; i < 40; i++)
                        {
                            Steps++;
                            float b = floor + i * (t3 - floor) / 40f;
                            float f = RM_TitanicKernel.SubLinearFactor(b, floor, minF);
                            Check(!float.IsNaN(f) && f >= minF - 1e-6f && f <= 1f + 1e-6f, $"factor {f} outside [{minF},1] at body {b}");
                            Check(f <= prevF + 1e-6f, $"factor rose with size ({prevB} -> {b})");
                            double want = Math.Min(1.0, Math.Max(minF, Math.Sqrt(floor / b)));
                            Check(Math.Abs(f - want) < 1e-5, $"factor {f} is not clamp(sqrt(floor/size)) = {want} at body {b} (the curve is sqrt, not linear)");
                            double total = b * f;
                            Check(total >= prevTotal - 1e-4, $"total yield fell as the beast grew ({prevB} -> {b}): sub-linear must still be increasing");
                            Check(f * b <= b + 1e-4, "yield above vanilla");
                            prevF = f; prevTotal = (float)total; prevB = b;
                        }
                        Check(Math.Abs(RM_TitanicKernel.SubLinearFactor(floor, floor, minF) - 1f) < 1e-6f, "exactly at the floor the factor must be 1");
                        // a pawn below its floor (a lifestage swell the other way) must not amplify
                        float lo = RM_TitanicKernel.SubLinearFactor(floor * 0.1f, floor, minF);
                        Check(Math.Abs(lo - 1f) < 1e-6f, "below the floor the factor must be 1, got " + lo);
                    }
                }
                catch (Exception e) { fails.Add($"yield seed {seed}: {e.Message}"); }
            }
            return fails;
        }

name: rimworld-load-round
description: How to spend a RimWorld cold load — and how to stop needing one. A 13-mod minimal list loads in 22 SECONDS against ~25 minutes on the owner's full list, making a full edit-build-deploy-test cycle about a minute; modlist_swap.py does the swap and restore. Covers what that minimal list cannot prove. Arriving already confident instead of "restart and see", writing the Player.log strings that will decide each item before launching, batching by ambiguity, what ModsConfig.xml is and is not authoritative about, src/RimMandrake/Utils/refresh.py and whether a load is needed at all, the shutdown window where companion DLLs deploy, the doctrine delta at launch, and harvesting the whole log. Use before calling or queueing a restart, when the game is about to close or has just launched, after any mod-list change, and whenever you are tempted to say "restart and see".
---

# The load round

A cold load costs **~23–30 minutes** and there is one game shared by five seats.
So a load is never spent on one question, and never spent to learn something that
could have been read off disk.

## 0. 🟢 FIRST: does this load have to be expensive at all?

**Measured 2026-08-19 — a cold load on a 13-mod MINIMAL list is 22 SECONDS**, against ~25
minutes on the owner's full list (576 as of 2026-08-20 — read
`ModsConfig.FULL.LATEST.xml`, never a number in a doc). The engine's own clock agrees:
`[RimBridge] STARTUP_TIMING phase=bridge-start.total elapsedMs=12364`. A quicktest world on
top costs **5 s**. ⇒ **the whole edit → build → deploy → launch → test cycle is about ONE
MINUTE.** Everything below about hoarding a load still applies to the owner's real stack —
but for *tool and mechanism* work the scarcity is gone. Do not spend a 25-minute load
proving something a 22-second one can prove.

⛔ **An XML-only change is proven by a MINIMAL-LIST RESTART, not by hot-reload
(owner's ruling 2026-09-03).** Deploy → restart minimal (22 s) → read back with
`jawa/get_defs`. **`jawa/hot_reload_defs` is retired as unstable** — it hung a
589-mod game for 5 minutes and left it unable to generate any pawn while every
health flag still read green. ⚠️ Its clean minimal-list pass (0.04 s, 2026-09-02)
was real and is *why* it is retired rather than gated: a call that behaves on 19
mods and destroys pawn generation on 589 cannot be trusted by the seat deciding
which case it is in. Canonical entry: `skills/rimworld-modding/SKILL.md` §2;
evidence: `infrastructure/state/items/closed/HOT_RELOAD_DEFS_BREAKS_PAWNGEN_1.md`.
Do not count it as a speed path in any test-time estimate either.

A **proof** never swaps the list or restarts the game itself: the `live-proof` runner
refuses `modlist_swap`, `modcheck run` and `deploy … --apply`. A proof declares the
smallest tier that holds its mod (`live-tier: <tier>`), and testq runs it on that list
(`skills/live-debugging-proof-harness/references/lightspeed-authoring.md` §2, §6).

```
python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/modlist_swap.py --status
python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/modlist_swap.py --minimal   # or --restore (separate runs; mutually exclusive); add --apply
```
`modlist_swap.py --restore` writes FULL.LATEST. After a `modset_builder.py --tier X --apply` swap,
`modset_builder.py --restore` puts back that swap's md5-verified before-copy instead (refuses if
there is none; `--restore-full` writes FULL.LATEST explicitly). Never mix the two families.
Plan-only by default; it archives the live file before every write. The owner's real list
is frozen at `infrastructure/state/modlists/ModsConfig.FULL.LATEST.xml`.

**The 13 and why each one is there:** harmony · core + all five expansions · VEF (Alpha
Biomes' hard dep) · `brrainz.rimbridgeserver` · alienworlds + tidallylocked · alphabiomes ·
mylittleplanet.
🔴 **Odyssey is NOT optional** — `Tile.Landmark` returns null without `OdysseyActive`, and
PlanetLayer/Orbit are Odyssey types. A leaner list silently has no landmarks.
🔴 **`brrainz.rimbridgeserver` is not optional** — without it there is no bridge at all,
however the companion DLL is deployed.

### Automated sweeps across many mod-list batches: `loadsweep/`

`src/RimMandrake/Utils/loadsweep/` (`gen_config.py` + `sweep_load.sh`) is a repo
tool that runs the write-config → restart-via-Steam → poll → grep-verdicts cycle
for you, ~60 s/cycle on the minimal list — feed it a batch file of extra
packageIds and it launches, waits, and prints the standing failure counts
(`config_errors`, `crossref_errors`, `patch_failed`, `typeload`, `recovery_hits`)
without you watching the load land.

⚠️ **Poll `"Bridge token:"` in `Player.log`, not the lazy JawaBench ready line.**
JawaBench's own "ready" marker only appears on the FIRST tool call
(`jawabench-init-line-is-lazy.md`), so waiting for it can hang a sweep forever on
a load that is actually up. `Bridge token:` is written at bridge start and is
the correct ready signal; `sweep_load.sh` also watches for `"Recovered from
incompatible or corrupted mods"` as the failure terminator.
🔴 Right after a relaunch that grep matches the PREVIOUS session's token until the
new process truncates `Player.log` — also require a shrunk size / small line count or
a newer mtime (`rimbridge/references/traps.md`, "`Player.log` PERSISTS between runs").
✅ **Don't hand-write that wait:** `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/logwait.py "Bridge token:" --timeout 900` counts only
text written after the call and needs no blind-scan override; in code open `logwait.LogCursor()` BEFORE the launch.
One command for the whole cycle (stop, tier, deploy, launch, wait, quicktest, run):
`src/RimMandrake/Utils/northstar_driver/live_session.py`.

⚠️ **A load stuck at 6 active mods (Core + five expansions) is RimWorld's own
corrupted-mods RECOVERY RESET, not your config write failing.** Check the log for
`"Resetting mods config and trying again"`. **The reset persists to disk** —
`ModsConfig.xml` now genuinely holds 6 mods — so rewrite your intended batch
before relaunching; retrying the same launch just reproduces the reset.

🟢 **Rapid QA win: sweep the ConfigError lines on every minimal/tier load, not
just a full one.** `Def.ConfigErrors()` runs after every patch and inheritance
resolve and catches real bugs offline `validate_patch.py` cannot see — measured
catching dead pawnkinds with no race (`RaceProperties` unresolved), a bad
`forcedMiss`, and thought stages out of `minSeverity` order, all in ~2 s on a
live load. `sweep_load.sh` already greps `^Config error in`; §8's
`harvest_log.py --show configerror` reads the same class of line on a full load
— read the mechanism note there (a config error means the def loaded and the
ENGINE disapproves, not necessarily that it's wrong for our purposes) before
filing anything this sweep surfaces.

### Which list to test on (owner rulings)

- **Small mod lists are the way to test until one final verification pass on the whole list** (owner, 2026-11-02): *"small mod lists should always be the way to test until a final verification pass on the whole huge mod list."*
- **Huge Things belongs on the testing mod lists** (owner, 2026-10-16): *"We also need to include the huge things mod in our testing mods too. We have so many huge things, we want to make sure we're always compatible with them."*

### ⚠️ What the minimal list CANNOT do

* **It cannot reproduce the 21,872-tile geometry.** `ferny.Worldbuilder` is absent, and
  Worldbuilder is what loads the TidallyLocked preset. A quicktest comes out 119,904 tiles.
  Anything depending on real tile IDs needs the full list.
* **It does not have the content mods.** A patch against a content mod (RimStarWars/Utinni/Mandrake) matches nothing there and logs nothing, so a PASS on minimal is UNMEASURED for it: such items need a dependency-complete item tier (`modset_builder.py --tier`) or the full list. A 21,872-row import validated at 81.6% on it, and
  **every** mismatch was one of 8 biome defs the 13-mod list lacks — not a tool defect.
* 🔴 **While it is installed, the live `ModsConfig.xml` is NOT evidence about the owner's
  stack.** A research thread read it and reported Gravship Exporter inactive; it is active
## 6. Building

- Target **.NET Framework 4.7.2** for RimWorld 1.4–1.6.
- Reference `Assembly-CSharp.dll` and the `UnityEngine.*` DLLs from
  `RimWorld/RimWorldWin64_Data/Managed/`.
- Set **Copy Local = false** on every game/Unity reference. Shipping
  `Assembly-CSharp.dll` inside your mod loads a second, stale copy of the entire
  game's types and produces failures that look like anything but their cause.
- Output the DLL to `<ModName>/1.6/Assemblies/`.
- Bump the assembly name when the mod is renamed; two loaded assemblies with the
  same name is its own confusing class of failure.

Decompile with dnSpy or ILSpy against that same `Assembly-CSharp.dll` when you
need to know what a method actually does. Reading the real IL is the C# analogue
of reading the real def, and it is equally non-optional.

---

## 7. Failure shapes and what they actually mean

| Log shape | Usual meaning |
|---|---|
| `Error in static constructor of X` | The mod is **dead** — nothing in it ran. Highest-priority finding in any log. |
| `ReflectionTypeLoadException` naming another mod's types | Load order (§2), not corruption. |
| `MissingMethodException: Constructor on type ... not found` | Entry-point signature (§4). Feature silently absent. |
| `Could not execute post-long-event action` + exception inside `LongEventHandler.ExecuteToExecuteWhenFinished` | **One queued action failed; the queue continues.** Verified from IL 2026-08-10 — per-action try/catch, the handler's `leave` targets the loop increment. Cost is that one action (usually one def's `ResolveIcon`). The *only* abort path is an NRE in the DeepProfiler block outside the try, which also bricks the queue behind "Already executing." |
| `AmbiguousMatchException` in a Harmony patch | The target method gained an overload in a game/mod update. The patcher is version-drifted. |
| Harmony patch applies but has no effect | Another mod's Prefix is returning `false` on the same method. |
| `Could not find type named X` in a def | The assembly didn't load, or the def references a class from a mod that isn't present. |

The pattern worth carrying between sessions: in a large stack, hard breaks
concentrate in **mods that reflect over other mods' types at startup** — patchers,
compatibility layers, indexers. They run early, they assume a shape, and the
shape changed. Grep for `static constructor` first, every time.

---
- **A subprocess-wrapping C# (`OracleClient.cs` style) must read both streams.** A real `claude -p` auth failure ('OAuth session expired') prints to STDOUT, so a wrapper that reads stderr only on a nonzero exit logs nothing useful; fall back to stdout when stderr is empty.
- **A native Burst-job crash with no managed exception is a native array freed too early, not the sounds logged just before it.** Seen on Stillsand 100x100 (4 of 4): a sun-cost path array in `RM_MapComponent_ShadeGrid` was freed one rebuild too early. Free retired native arrays only after 60 ticks (`RM_DeferredDisposal`); live-confirmed over 12,084 ticks, one run.
- **A float-times-int in a `Ceil` can overshoot:** `0.3f*100` ceils to 31, moving a 30% floor by one HP. Keep thresholds as whole percents and compare `hp*100 > max*pct`.
- **Never scribe a LOCAL list/set in `ExposeData`.** `List<T> list = Saving ? copy : null; Scribe_Collections.Look(ref list, ...)` with `owned = new(list)` in `PostLoadInit` loses the data: the list is filled in LoadingVars and the local is gone by `PostLoadInit`. Scribe the field itself (`Scribe_Collections.Look(ref hashSetField, label, LookMode.Value)` has a HashSet overload) and null-guard it in `PostLoadInit`.
- **`FleeUtility.FleeJob(pawn, threat, fleeDistance)` aims for a total SEPARATION of `fleeDistance`** (it moves `fleeDistance - distanceToThreat`), not a step. A fixed distance at or below the threat's current distance sends the pawn nowhere or toward it; use `max(base, dist + margin)`.
- **Unverified: `Verse.SandGrid` may ignore depth writes on Sand/SoftSand or `holdSnowOrSand=false` terrain** (claimed by a GPT review). If true, `RM_DuneTrackEraser.ProofErase`/`ProofEraseByWeather` (which pick the first standable track-surface cell) would read a false `erased=False` and the eraser itself would fail on such cells. Decompile `SandGrid.SetDepth/AddDepth` before trusting either probe's `erased=False`.
- **On .NET Framework 4.7.2 / Mono, `List<T>.Reverse()` and `Array.Reverse(Array)` on a non-primitive struct element type fall back to GetValue/SetValue and box every element.** A net8 selftest allocation count (`GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread`) cannot see it; in a zero-alloc hot path swap by hand.

## 8. A csproj with `EnableDefaultCompileItems false` needs the new file listed twice

⚠️ **A project that sets `EnableDefaultCompileItems false` and lists every
`.cs` file explicitly** — `RM_CreatureBehaviors.csproj` lists all ~75 files
this way — **compiles a new file dropped into `Source/` into NOTHING, with no
error.** The class simply does not exist at runtime, and every def
referencing it then fails to resolve for a reason that points nowhere near the
missing `<Compile Include>` line. ⇒ Adding a `.cs` file to such an assembly is
always a two-file change: the source file, and the csproj's file list.
(2026-09-23)

## 9. Job drivers and think nodes that silently swallow a custom job or state

**A job that "starts then reverts to Wait after 60 ticks" is usually the
DRIVER killing it, not the target.** Read the job driver's `FailOn`/
`AddFailCondition` lines in source before blaming the thing the pawn was
aimed at — `JobDriver_Refuel.cs` kills any unforced job when its auto-refuel
gating says no. A companion mod fixed this class of bug by setting
`job.playerForced` on the jobs it hands out. (2026-09-09)

**`Pawn.CurrentlyUsableForBills()` requires `InBed()` for EVERY pawn
billGiver** (surgery, memory wipe, any whole-pawn `Recipe_Surgery`-style
bill). A droid-type pawn never satisfies this: `needsRest=false` gives it no
drive to seek a bed, and `WorkGiver_TakeToBedToOperate` explicitly refuses any
pawn with `RaceProps.IsFlesh==false`. This silently blocks **every**
whole-pawn recipe on a non-fleshy race, not just whichever one happens to be
under test. Fix: a Harmony prefix on `CurrentlyUsableForBills` that skips the
`InBed()` check for non-fleshy pawns specifically, keeping the
`InteractionCell` reachability check. (2026-09-12, `DROIDWORKS_WIPE_SEVERITY_1`)

**Two think nodes dispatch mental states and only one of them is
subclass-aware.** `ThinkNode_ConditionalMentalState` tests

# Engine facts measured in this project (ticking, MayRequire, csproj, patches)

Moved from the project `CLAUDE.md` on 2026-10-11 (weekly cleaning), text unchanged except heading levels. CLAUDE.md keeps a one-line rule and points here. Entries state what IS: delete a line the moment it turns false, never annotate it.

- 🔴 **`Plant` never overrides `Tick()` — only `TickLong()`.** A `ThingComp` attached to a
  `PlantBase`-derived def (via `<comps>`) must override `CompTickLong()`, never `CompTick()`,
  or it will likely never fire at all: `ThingWithComps.TickLong()` is what loops
  `comps[i].CompTickLong()`, and nothing schedules the Normal ticker for a plant. This also
  means the engine's own Long-ticker cadence already throttles the comp — do not add a manual
  `IsHashIntervalTick` gate on top of it (RimSage-confirmed against decompiled 1.6 source,
  2026-09-27, building `RM_CompPlantPredator`/`MIASMA_SCUTTLER_PREDATION_1`).

## Patch and def behaviour

- **A patch that matches nothing logs nothing.** `PatchOperationConditional` and
  `PatchOperationFindMod` both return true on no match.
- 🔴 **`MayRequire` on a top-level `<Operation>` node is IGNORED by the decompiled
  1.6 engine — it does nothing.** Two patches (`RUT_Bitumen_KorvethSource.xml`,
  `RUT_ThrummelSeepwax_RosterSource.xml`, added `6714ad67c`) each carried
  `<Operation MayRequire="mandrake.rm.thesump">` to guard a recipe that pays with a
  TheSump-only item — TheSump is not in the canonical mod list, so the intent
  was "skip this patch when TheSump is absent." The guard is silently inert: both
  applied anyway, the ingredient resolved null, and `RecipeDefGenerator.SetIngredients`
  NREd → RimWorld's own corrupted-mods recovery **reset `ModsConfig.xml` to
  Core-only**, live-hit twice in one night (2026-09-27) before this was found. Same
  failure shape as `MODCHECK_DONOR_ENVIRONMENTS_1`'s Armoury/ModularWeapons2 case.
  ⇒ **`MayRequire` only works on the elements it's documented for** (a `<li>` inside
  a list, a `ModExtension`, a `ThingDef`'s own attribute) — never assume it gates a
  whole `<Operation>` block; guard with `PatchOperationFindMod`/`Conditional` instead,
  or (the fix actually applied) test that the referenced def actually exists before
  applying. MEASURED 2026-10-09: **0** live top-level `<Operation MayRequire>` remain in
  `src/` and all 14 `<li>`-level attributes resolve (census of that date).
  ⚠️ A composed member (e.g. `mandrake.rm.longshade`) has a standalone About.xml in `src/` but
  **no packageId at runtime** — its id is folded into `mandrake.rm.biomes`, so a `MayRequire`
  naming a member id silently never loads (sitting 2 found 26 such sites).

- ⚠️ **`RM_CreatureBehaviors.csproj` sets `EnableDefaultCompileItems false` and lists every file.** A new
  `.cs` in `Source/` without a `<Compile Include>` line **compiles into nothing, with no error**. Adding a
  file to that assembly is always a two-file change.
- **The global `RM_JobGiver_ShadeHop` (Animal_PreWander prio 10) outranks `RM_ShadeSeekingWanderExtension` on a sun-heat map** and dashes every wild animal across open sun to the next shade patch on a HEATSTROKE budget. A creature with its own sun clock (`RM_LoommaSunstruck`, `ShadeDrivenSeverity`) must opt out with `RM_SunDashExtension` `rangeFactor 0`; do not exempt it, which also kills SunEscape.
- **Research 'same view coords' ConfigErrors compare the private `ResearchProjectDef` `x,y`, not `researchViewX/Y`.** Dubs Bad Hygiene Lite's C# writes `x,y` for four projects in Lite mode (ModernFixtures 0,0; HotTubs 1,0; AdvancedShowers 2,0; AdvancedToilets 3,0), so an XML pin on those four reaches nothing the check reads: move the neighbour instead. Def dump rows hold both pairs.
- **Sea-floor LAYER maps use the floor BiomeDef (`RM_SeabedFloor_<Sea>`), not the sea's,** so anything a sea owns reaches its floor only if `RM_SeabedFloorLife.CopyLife` copies it (floors had `maxFishPopulation 0`, so no ship-reached floor could fish). Add every new sea-owned BiomeDef field there.
- **Before moving an SWBestiary port to the RM tier, grep for an `RM_` twin of the same creature** (`git grep '<defName>RM_<Stem>'` and the `RSW_` name in src/RimMandrake headers): the Q1 tier move already made `RM_Vozzik` and `RM_Vekka` (=`RSW_SandLion`) in Stillsand while leaving `RSW_` originals for the frozen Utinni `RUT_ExtremeDesert`. That is a dedupe (retire the `RSW_` copy, alias `RSW_`->`RM_`, repoint Utinni), not a name clash. Also check for `Class="RimMandrake.StarWars.*"` comps: the def cannot leave SWB until that C# lives in an RM assembly.
- **`RM_HediffComp_EnvironmentalExposure`'s salinity bands (`freshMultiplier` 0.8, `brineMultiplier` 0.6 by default) apply on ANY map with `RM_MapComponent_GradientAxis`, not on Miasma only as the code comment says.** Every exposure hediff that leaves them unset runs slower than its `severityPerDayExposed` (measured on the Scald: 0.48/day for 0.6). Set both to 1 unless the hazard really is salinity-driven.
- **Before deleting a patch whose effect 'was folded elsewhere', prove the target def's `texPath` still resolves to a real file.** Deleting a donor-name patch left `RM_Zhissa` and `RM_Bulloo` INVISIBLE (no texPath). Patch-cleanup agents must prove effect survival per def, not by a header comment.
- **FlowWorks `CanBuildOnTerrain` has several postfixes that only ever flip false->true** (`RM_Patch_SuspensionAffordance` lends Light on timber/steel/heavy decks; `RM_Patch_FlowDoorOnWetCanal`). A refusal rule on that gate must be `[HarmonyPriority(Priority.Last)]` or a timber deck re-admits what it refused.
- **Vanilla `MapDrawer.WholeMapChanged` has no null guard on sections (`MapMeshDirty` has one).** Calling it on a map whose drawer was never built (e.g. a load that threw in FinalizeLoading) NREs; dirty cells through `MapMeshDirty` instead (as Cauldron `RM_VentGas.ClearAll` does).
- **FlowWorks hose shaping must judge a drawn pose with `HoseMath.BodyGap >= BodyHalf`, not `HoseMath.Clear`,** which judges only the CENTRELINE (grazes to 0.06 inside a wall); a stage accepting on Clear alone can draw half the hose width over a wall corner (the nozzle lead-out Dubins join did, 25/40 seeds). Test with an independent wall ruler (`HoseDrawGeometryChecks.cs`). Measured residue 6/172: a nozzle pointed within ~2 cells of a wall end has no minimum-radius join that clears, and the owner-ruled straight lead-out can itself graze a corner (placement, not bend).
- **A hose meeting a port from the SIDE (lead-out cell blocked) cannot be re-aimed onto the port axis by a Hermite** (`HoseMath.EndOnPort` loops back behind the end); draw an elbow instead (`HoseMath.PortFitting`: coupling face slides <=0.1 into the building, wrap cut to the join). SideArrival = last 0.5 cell >35 deg off the axis.
- **A mod that changes passability by PATH GRID only (FlowWorks R12 deep swim patches `PathGrid.CalculatedCostAt`) silently changes every mod that reads `pathGrid.Walkable` as 'solid ground'** (GSS's cord snapshot lost its water stubs). Classify terrain by its def (passability, `IsWater`) when the question is 'can something lie on it', not 'can a pawn cross it'.
- **`RM_FluidIdentity.FluidOfTerrain` answers null for any LiquidDef with no `canalFluid`** (salt water, brine, acid, the coloured waters) and `FormBody` falls back to `RM_Fluid_Water`, so every 'is this body water?' gate (`DepthModelApplies`, sameFluid body merge) treats a sea or brine strip as fresh water (P14 drawdown restaged salt ponds onto the freshwater ladder and thirst drank them as potable). Gate on the registry LiquidDef (`RM_LiquidBottleUtility.LiquidAt(t).canalFluid`), not `body.fluid`. sameFluid still merges salt with fresh (open).
- **Vanilla 1.6 `GenStep_Animals` loops while `!AnimalEcosystemFull` and BREAKS on the first `SpawnRandomWildAnimalAt` that returns false.** One empty pick (no season-acceptable kind with commonality > 0 at the random cell, e.g. the Biotech pollution path using `CommonalityOfPollutionAnimal` on a biome with none) gives zero animals of every kind. `DesiredAnimalDensity` reads `tile.biome.animalDensity` x mutators, not `map.Biome` alone. Static check for the Scrub: `LeaningScrub/selftest_scrub_wildlife_zero_paths.py`.
- **ExplosiveGrowth: a roster row's `top` is silently void when `RM_ExplosiveGrowthRegistry` makes the plant Exempt.** That happens when `growDays` < `minGrowDaysToSoak` (1) and the row decides no archetype or `fireAdapted`: top becomes None, `Fire/ResolveOutcome` does nothing and logs nothing. A short-lived plant given a top needs an archetype or `fireAdapted` on its row (`RM_FE_Plant_ScorchFruit`, growDays 0.05, needed `fireAdapted`); `selftest_explosivegrowth_top_donors.py` pins the donors.
- **Forge wild dhuvvox are rare.** Vanilla `WildAnimalSpawner` arithmetic (W = area*density/10000; expected count = W*c_k/sum(c_j*e_j)) gives 0.9-2.1 per map and 0.1-0.2 groups, so most Forge maps start with none and the Rain's EruptSwarm (60) usually lands with no resident anchor, i.e. anywhere unroofed. Measure a roster's per-kind count with the method of `TheForge/selftest_dhuvvox_swarm_budget.py` before arguing a population needs aggregation or more weight.
- **Before calling a comp class unused, grep its full name across all of `src/` (RimMandrake, RimUtinni, RimStarWars), Defs AND Patches.** `RM_CompHeatPusherGated` looked unused but `RUT_Radiothermal.xml` names it as `compClass`. `lint_ticker_compat` now merges comps a `Patches/` PatchOperationAdd puts on a def (and patched `tickerType`), and its PAWN_DOUBLE_PUSH check fails any pawn carrying vanilla `CompHeatPusher(Powered)` or a subclass with no `CompTickRare` override.
- **A registry row whose only surface presence is a herd/unbounded token is not a count.** Marking it `SurfacePlaced` zeroes its vanilla scatter while the placer reads the token as no value, so its veins vanish everywhere. `Placeable` requires a positive EPM number in some biome (`RM_MineralSurfaceKernel.cs`).
- **Base RimWorld and all five DLCs ship no net item, net verb or net class.** 'Use the game's net mechanics' has to be built from vanilla Projectile flight plus `ShotReport.HitFactorFromShooter`. Also, vanilla `Projectile.ImpactSomething` hits `usedTarget.Thing` wherever it has moved (bullets effectively home once the hit is rolled), so target speed matters only if you launch at a CELL and judge the landing yourself.
- **A pit-cover deck (4-way connected `RM_PitCover_*` lids) springs at its WEAKEST lid's rating** (`CompPitCoverTrigger.RunScan`): swapping one cell of a woven-scrap deck to planks still rates 40 kg, so a test that needs a lid to hold must relay the whole deck. A per-cell mock hides this; mocks must model the deck rule.
- ⚠️ **FlowWorks' `RimMandrake_FlowWorks.csproj` also sets `EnableDefaultCompileItems false`.** A new `Source/*.cs` referenced only from XML builds into nothing and `winbuild.py` still says BUILT. full review, `Transient/hugethingsbounds2026-10-07/` (gone; never kept in git)).

## spec (as built, FOUNDRY 2026-10-21; engine-only, no creature or faction named)

- **Scavenger draw** (`CorpseSiteVisitors.DrawScavengers`, in `Building_TitanicCorpseSite`'s daily step): a daily chance
  (default 35%) brings 1..max (default 3) wild predators the map's own biomes home, adult tier None, season-survivable,
  from a map edge to the site. Count never exceeds what the meat left can feed for a day (`RM_TitanicKernel.ScavengerCount`).
- **Camps** (`CorpseSiteVisitors.MakeCamp`): a daily chance (default 10%) brings 2-4 people of a non-hostile humanlike
  faction; vanilla `LordJob_VisitColony` with the chill spot beside the site for `corpseSiteCampHours` (default 36), then
  they leave. Letter on arrival.
- **Eating**: each scavenger/camper within 10 cells of the site takes `corpseSiteVisitorMeatPerDay` (default 20) meat a day
  (`RM_TitanicKernel.VisitorTake`). Inspect line shows who is at the remains.
- **Titan passage** (`IncidentDef RM_TitanPassage`, `IncidentWorker_TitanPassage`, `MapComponent_TitanPassages`): picks a
  race of adult tier T2/T3 from this map biome's explicit passage hints, else its own roster, with sea/land matching (`RM_TitanicKernel.TitanEventEligible`,
  also the one-T3-per-map spacing law); "Footfall tremors" letter naming the edge; camera shake every 300 ticks rising
  0.3 -> 1.5 and a message every 2 h through `titanEventWarningHours` (default 2, owner 2026-11-11); then the titan spawns and walks edge to
  edge on a vanilla `LordJob_ExitMapNear` (the herd-migration shape). Re-checked at arrival; if no longer eligible the
  tremors "fade".
- Mod Settings: scavengers / camps toggles + chance, max, meat/day, camp hours under the corpse-site group; a new "Titan
  events" group with its toggle and warning hours. The warning default is owner-ruled at two hours (2026-11-11); valid explicit player tuning remains supported. Other numbers remain **PROVISIONAL** (FOUNDRY first guess, to be tuned live).

## criteria

- A1 L0: `validation.py` STATIC PASS with the new needles; titanic fuzz family `visitors` 0 failures; HugeThings selftests green.
- A2 L2: on a map with a T3 corpse site, scavenger chance 100%, `DebugDailyStep` -> ScavengerCount > 0 (predators of the map's biome, none tiered); after they reach the site the next step lowers MeatRemaining by VisitorsEatenTotal's increase.
- A3 L2: camp chance 100%, `DebugDailyStep` -> CamperCount > 0 under a non-hostile faction's VisitColony lord; they leave after corpseSiteCampHours.
- A4 L2: firing RM_TitanPassage on a map whose own passage hints/roster supplies an eligible titan -> HasPending true and a tremor letter; DebugArriveNow -> LastArrived spawned, tier >= T2, kind from that map biome's passage hints/roster with seaMatch=True, with an ExitMapNear lord; with a T3 already on the map a T3 is never chosen.
- A5 L2: each new toggle off removes exactly its effect (no draw / no camp / CanFireNow false).
- A6 L4: the owner sees a passage and a scavenged site in play and judges the feel and the numbers.

# Delegated design judgment: juvenile passage classification and T3 spacing

This is a delegated design decision, not owner approval. It authorizes no roster evictions and no combat changes.

## Verdict

| Concern | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Event classification (`AdultTier`, base × max(1, largest factor)) | **KEEP** |
| T3 spacing (currently keyed on `AdultTier == T3`) | **REDO, bounded** |
| `DefQualifies` comp attachment (floor 1) | **KEEP**, separate purpose |
| Runtime `GetTier` (actual `Pawn.BodySize`) | **KEEP** |

## Reasons

**1. Eligibility must stay on the grown tier.** The owner said "Calves are ok", and the implemented note reads "juveniles stay (adult tier)". The card was about juvenile kinds.
- Switching eligibility to the maximum supported size would evict calves whenever base × 0.5 falls below T2.
  - Any juvenile-only race with an inherited base between 8 and 16 drops to T1 under the default ladder.
  - `RM_ReefbackJuv` (supported size 16) drops to T1 under a valid custom ladder such as 4/18/30.
- That would quietly change calf eligibility, which is forbidden.
- So the `adultTier >= T2` gate stays exactly as it is.

**2. Spacing should measure what the arrival can actually be.**
- The spacing law is "one T3 per map", and `T3OnMap` counts actual T3s using `GetTier`.
- A race whose every valid stage has a factor below 1 can never produce a T3 pawn by life stage. An arrived `RM_ReefbackJuv` (16) never counts toward `T3OnMap`.
- Blocking it as though it were T3 enforces a cap on something it can never become.
- Using the maximum supported size for spacing only ever relaxes spacing for juvenile-only races. It never removes eligibility, because the spacing tier is always ≤ `AdultTier` under the fallback rules below.

**3. No other gate changes.** Sea/land matching, biome pool/list, opt-out, season, `harnessOnly`, Animal/Dryad, `HasPending` and the arrival recheck all stay as they are.

## Policy (bounded)

- **Eligibility tier:** `AdultTier(race)`, unchanged. It is `TierFor(base × max(1, largest non-null factor), ladder, force)`.

- **New spacing tier, `SpacingTier(race)`:** this equals `TierFor(base × m, ladder, force)`, where `m` is the largest stage factor. It applies only when the stage list is well-formed:
  - the list is non-null and non-empty;
  - every entry and its `def` are non-null;
  - every factor is finite and > 0.

  In every other case, `SpacingTier = AdultTier`. Any malformed data falls back to the conservative tier, which blocks.
  - When `m ≥ 1`, the two tiers are identical by construction. This covers factors above 1.
  - The fallback covers: missing, empty or null lists; null entries or defs; factor 0, negative, NaN or ±∞.

- **Kernel change:** `TitanEventEligible(adultTier, spacingTier, …)` keeps `adultTier < T2 → false`. The spacing clause becomes `!(spacingTier == T3 && t3OnMap)`.
  - Update both doc comments from "when it is itself T3" to "when any supported life stage of it can be T3".
  - Put the stage fold in the Verse-free kernel so the self-test can cover it.

- **Force overrides:** the same `ForceOf` value applies to both tiers.
  - Force-out gives None, so the kind is ineligible.
  - Force-in floors at T1, which is still below T2, so force-in alone never makes a passage titan.
  - Force-in never lifts spacing above the natural size tier.
  - Force-out pawns do not count toward `T3OnMap`. This is current behavior and is kept.

- **Thresholds:** both tiers read `Thresholds` at call time.
  - A disabled, equal, descending, NaN or infinite custom ladder falls back to the shipped 4/8/20.
  - Boundaries are inclusive (`>=`), matching `GetTier`. 32 × 0.5 = 16 is exact in float, so a custom T3 of 16 makes the juvenile spacing tier T3, and a live juvenile at 16 counts as an actual T3.

- **Caches:** do not cache tiers, because the ladder can change at runtime. Preferably cache nothing new; the loop is cheap, and a cache would mask fixture mutations.
  - `cachedThresholds` (shipped def) and `seaCache` (per kind) are unaffected.
  - `DefQualifies` is startup-only; crossing T1 still needs a restart, and that is unrelated to passage tiers.

- **Runtime-only size changes:** these are out of scope. `GetTier` remains the runtime authority, and `T3OnMap` keeps reading live sizes.
  - The def-level spacing tier cannot foresee mod, gene or hediff body-size changes. This caveat is recorded, not solved.

- **Comp attachment:** `DefQualifies` keeps its conservative floor 1 because it decides comp presence, not event tier. Do not reuse `SpacingTier` there.

## Expected matrix (other gates true)

Default ladder 4/8/20 unless stated.

| Case | AdultTier | SpacingTier | GetTier per stage | Eligible, t3 false | Eligible, t3 true |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary base 32, factors .2/.5/1 | T3 | T3 | 6.4→T1, 16→T2, 32→T3 | yes | **no** (unchanged) |
| Same race, calf pawn on map | n/a | n/a | T1 | does not set t3OnMap | n/a |
| Juvenile-only base 32, factors .2/.5 | T3 | **T2** | T1, T2 | yes | **yes** (currently no) |
| Juvenile-only, custom 4/8/16 | T3 | T3 | T1, **T3** | yes | no |
| Juvenile-only, custom 4/18/30 | T3 | T1 | T1, T1 | **yes** (calf kept) | yes |
| Juvenile-only, custom 4/8/40 | T2 | T2 | T1, T2 | yes | yes |
| Base 3, factor 4 | T2 | T2 | 12→T2 | yes | yes |
| Base 3, factor 4, custom 4/8/12 | T3 | T3 | T3 | yes | no |
| Null or empty list, base 32 | T3 | T3 (fallback) | not spawnable (L0 only) | yes | no |
| Juvenile list + null entry/def | T3 | T3 (fallback) | n/a | yes | no |
| Juvenile list + factor 0, negative or NaN | T3 | T3 (fallback) | n/a | yes | no |
| Factor +∞, base > 0 | T3 (current, kept) | T3 | ∞→T3 | yes | no |
| Force-out (any size) | None | None | None | no | no |
| Force-in, base 1 | T1 | T1 | T1 | no | no |
| Invalid custom ladder (equal, descending, NaN, ∞, disabled) | shipped-ladder results | shipped-ladder results | shipped-ladder results | as default rows | as default rows |

## Broadened scenarios to cover

1. **Roster census (L0 and L1).** For every `PawnKindDef`, record `AdultTier`, `SpacingTier` and `DefQualifies`.
   - List every juvenile-only race, including `RM_SiltLampreyJuv` and the other Miasma-nursery young.
   - Flag any whose supported tier is below T2 while `AdultTier ≥ T2`. These are the calves that maximum-supported eligibility would have evicted. Their eligibility must be unchanged.
2. **Inherited-def verification (L1).** Confirm that the loaded `RM_ReefbackJuv` really has exactly two stages (Baby 0.2, Juvenile 0.5) and base 32 after `Inherit="False"`.
   - Confirm whether it inherits any `RM_TitanicExtension`, `forceEnabled` or `harnessOnly` from its parent.
3. **Lineage depends on the inherited base.** A juvenile def that overrides `baseBodySize` downward loses grown-tier eligibility, because there is no parent link. The census should flag any such def; do not fix it here.
4. **Ordinary-race arrivals may generate as calves.** Spacing still blocks the race, because some stage can be T3. This is the conservative intent.
5. **Arrival recheck.** If a passage is scheduled with no T3 and a T3 appears before arrival, it fades. If the ladder changes between scheduling and arrival, the recheck uses the new ladder. Both behaviors are unchanged.
6. **What `T3OnMap` counts.** Downed, tamed and player T3s count. Dead, unspawned or carried pawns and corpse-sites do not. All unchanged.
7. **Juvenile arrival beside a T3.** This now yields one T3 plus a T2 titan on the map. The draft "T2 count capped low" is not implemented, and none is invented here.

## Negative controls (all must hold)

- `Eligible(k, map, false)` is identical before and after the change for every kind on every representative map.
- `Eligible(k, map, true)` changes only by adding kinds where `AdultTier == T3` and `SpacingTier < T3`.
- `DefQualifies` and `GetTier` are identical across the census.
- Ordinary Reefback with t3 true stays ineligible.
- A juvenile-only race with a malformed list and t3 true stays ineligible.
- A juvenile-only race fails as before on: a land map, an opted-out biome, being off the passage list or unhomed, the season gate, or force-out.
- Under the default ladder, a live `RM_ReefbackJuv` juvenile (16) leaves `T3OnMap` false.

## L1 proof bounds

- Use loaded-method reads and predicate calls only, on a fresh deployed process: `GetTier`, `AdultTier`, `SpacingTier`, the kernel predicate, and `Eligible` with explicit `t3OnMap`.
- Build malformed cases from synthetic in-memory defs that are never added to `DefDatabase`. Prefer this over mutating real defs; if a real def is touched, restore it field-exactly.
- Restore every setting changed (custom-tier toggle, T1/T2/T3) to its exact prior value, and record before/after values.
- Do not claim any passage, crossing, flight or L4 acceptance. Spawn nothing that flies.

## Remaining caveats

- The owner ruled on calves, not on spacing. Spacing is a BENCH law, so refining it is delegated design. If the owner meant "a juvenile titan counts as a titan for spacing", that would reverse this decision; no evidence says so.
- `AdultTier` treats a +∞ factor as T3, while the kernel's `DefQualifies` guards ∞ to 1. Only malformed data is affected; this is recorded, not changed.
- Body-size modifiers outside factor × base are unconfirmed (the existing `GetTier` open question). Def-level spacing cannot anticipate them.

"""host_guard.py - one driver per game, per MACHINE, for scripts as well as windows (BRIDGE_LOCK_WIDEN_ONE_PER_HOST).

Two machines each run a RimWorld: Archmagi (the interactive lane) and SteveDesktop (the batch test centre). Each
machine's game has exactly one guard: that machine's own process-keyed driver lock (driver_lock.py, the file
`rmpaths scratch/DRIVER_LOCK.json` on THAT machine's data root). `rimflow bridge take` already takes it for a window;
this module lets a SCRIPT take the same lock - the testq worker, the dispatcher's Archmagi backfill, modcheck,
deploy and rw_game.sh - so a window and a script can never both drive one game.

  * The holder of a script take is the script's OWN process (not the nearest `claude` ancestor, which is what a
    window's take uses): the guard is fenced to the process doing the driving and frees the moment it exits.
  * Children inherit the take: a holder exports RM_HOST_GUARD_GEN=<generation> (and adds it to WSLENV so a Windows
    python.exe child sees it); a nested acquire whose generation matches the live lock is a no-op pass-through. So
    `host_guard.py run -- worker` -> rw_game.sh -> modcheck all count as one driver.
  * On Archmagi a script also refuses while the cross-clone shared bridge file names a live window holder, because
    a window that took the bridge before the driver lock existed, or from the other clone, is still driving.
  * A take made from ANOTHER machine (Archmagi taking SteveDesktop's game for an interactive session) carries that
    machine's identity; driver_lock reads it as "not inspectable" and its heartbeat decides (45 min).

  * 🔴 His OWNER hold lives in this lock too, as `seat: OWNER`, so it binds the clone whose ledger has not seen it:
    neither a take nor --force passes a held OWNER lock (owner, by card 2026-10-30: "45 minutes after my last interaction, or I
    deliberately release it"). This machine cannot measure his interactions, so only a caller that has can pass:
    `rimflow bridge take --host` runs his rule and hands its verdict over as --owner-cleared. A lock with its process
    gone and its heartbeat 45 min old is free here as any other; `rimflow bridge take` still runs his rule on it first
    (HOST_OWNER_HOLD_ENFORCE_ACROSS_CLONES).

CLI (exit 0 ok, 75 held by someone else, 2 usage or lock unusable):
  host_guard.py status [--json]
  host_guard.py take    --seat S --for WHAT [--identity-json J] [--force WHY] [--owner-cleared VERDICT [--owner-heartbeat T]]
  host_guard.py release --seat S [--identity-json J] [--force WHY] [--owner-cleared VERDICT]
  host_guard.py run     --seat S --for WHAT [--force WHY] [--owner-cleared VERDICT] -- CMD [ARGS...]   hold for CMD's life
  host_guard.py remote  HOST status|take|release [same flags]                run it on HOST over ssh
"""
import argparse
import contextlib
import json
import os
import shlex
import socket
import subprocess
import sys

try:                                   # imported as rimflow.host_guard (cli.py) - one copy of model, not two
    from . import driver_lock
except ImportError:                    # run as a script on the runner or from a shell
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    import driver_lock  # noqa: E402

ENV_GEN = "RM_HOST_GUARD_GEN"
EX_HELD = 75
# How a host is reached over ssh from the dispatching machine. Only SteveDesktop is remote today.
SSH_TARGETS = {"stevedesktop": os.environ.get("STEVE_WSL", "mandrake@stevedesktop-wsl")}
RUNNER_DIR = os.environ.get("RM_RUNNER_DIR", "~/rm/runner")


def _model():
    """Late import: model pulls the ledger paths, which a bare `status` on the runner does not need."""
    if __package__:
        from . import model
    else:
        import model
    return model


def local_machine():
    """This machine's key (RM_HOST overrides the hostname), or None when it is not a known game host."""
    name = (os.environ.get("RM_HOST") or socket.gethostname()).strip().lower()
    return name if name in _model().BRIDGE_HOSTS else None


def local_host():
    """This process's bridge key: the machine, plus RM_GAME_INSTANCE when that names a second game ('stevedesktop.b')."""
    machine = local_machine()
    inst = (os.environ.get("RM_GAME_INSTANCE") or "").strip().lower()
    return "%s.%s" % (machine, inst) if machine and inst not in ("", "a") else machine


@contextlib.contextmanager
def instance_env(inst):
    """Aim lock_path() at game `inst` (None: today's) for the block; a shell on one game may take another's lock by name.
    The game this process already means changes nothing, so a lock path a selftest pinned stays pinned."""
    have = (os.environ.get("RM_GAME_INSTANCE") or "").strip().lower()
    if (have if have != "a" else "") == (inst or ""):
        yield
        return
    saved = {k: os.environ.get(k) for k in ("RM_GAME_INSTANCE", "RIMFLOW_DRIVER_LOCK")}
    try:
        if inst:
            import game_instance
            os.environ["RM_GAME_INSTANCE"] = inst
            os.environ["RIMFLOW_DRIVER_LOCK"] = game_instance.lock_path(inst)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.environ["RIMFLOW_DRIVER_LOCK"]), exist_ok=True)
        else:
            os.environ.pop("RM_GAME_INSTANCE", None)
            os.environ.pop("RIMFLOW_DRIVER_LOCK", None)
        yield
    finally:
        for k, v in saved.items():
            if v is None:
                os.environ.pop(k, None)
            else:
                os.environ[k] = v


def lock_path():
    return driver_lock.lock_path()


def self_identity():
    """The identity of THIS process - a script's guard is fenced to the script, not to the window that started it."""
    me = dict(driver_lock.my_identity())
    pid = os.getpid()
    me["pid"] = pid
    me["start"] = driver_lock._win_start(pid) if os.name == "nt" else driver_lock._proc_start(pid)
    return me


def _reentrant(path):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start, stop and query the test-centre RimWorld on SteveDesktop. Runs in SteveDesktop's WSL
# (from Archmagi: ssh mandrake@stevedesktop-wsl ~/rm/runner/infrastructure/stevedesktop/rw_game.sh up).
#
#   rw_game.sh status         running? pid, session, bridge port from Player.log
#   rw_game.sh up [--wait]    start the game unless running; --wait blocks until the bridge
#                             announces its port in a Player.log written after the launch (max 600 s)
#   rw_game.sh down           graceful taskkill, then /F after 90 s
#   rw_game.sh init           renew the test companion profile; seed Prefs.xml if it lacks
#                             runInBackground True (game must be stopped for that half)
#
# Every verb acts on one game: RM_GAME_INSTANCE=b rw_game.sh down stops b and only b; nothing set is
# game a, as ever (src/RimMandrake/Utils/game_instance.py finds a game by its command line and stops
# it by pid). A named game's `up` starts it directly, its `init` seeds it even with game a up.
#
# STEVEDESKTOP_LAUNCH_WIRE_DESKTOP_SESSION (2026-10-25). Why it looks like this:
#  - The game on SteveDesktop is ours outright (owner, 2026-10-25: "Steve no longer plays
#    Rimworld ... this game is ours to play with"). It runs with its normal save-data folder
#    (sjlewis's LocalLow), so ModsConfig.xml, Prefs.xml and Saves there belong to the runner.
#  - The game is started by running RimWorldWin64.exe directly; Steam must be running, and `up`
#    starts it (logged in by its remembered account) when it is not.
#  - powershell.exe is reached by its full /mnt/c path: a Tailscale SSH session has no Windows
#    dirs on PATH. Started from WSL interop, the process lands in session 1 (the logged-in
#    desktop), which is where a Unity game must run; from Windows OpenSSH it would land in
#    session 0 with no display.
#  - Paths come from testcentre_env.sh (RM_STEAMAPPS, RM_GAME_USERDATA, RM_GAME_LOGDIR).
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
[ -n "${RM_STEAMAPPS:-}" ] || . "$HERE/testcentre_env.sh"
GI="$HERE/../../src/RimMandrake/Utils/game_instance.py"
NAMED=
case "${RM_GAME_INSTANCE:-a}" in
    a|A) ;;
    *) _env=$(python3 "$GI" env) || exit 2; eval "$_env"; NAMED=$RM_GAME_INSTANCE ;;   # after testcentre_env.sh: b's folders win
esac
PS=$(command -v powershell.exe || echo /mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe)
winpath() { echo "$1" | sed -E 's#^/mnt/([a-z])/#\U\1:/#; s#/#\\#g'; }
GAME_WSL="$RM_STEAMAPPS/common/RimWorld"
EXE_WIN=$(winpath "$GAME_WSL/RimWorldWin64.exe")
DIR_WIN=$(winpath "$GAME_WSL")
DATA_WIN=$(winpath "$RM_GAME_USERDATA")
STEAM_EXE_WIN=$(winpath "$(dirname "$RM_STEAMAPPS")")\\steam.exe
LOG="$RM_GAME_LOGDIR/Player.log"

ps_q() { "$PS" -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "\$ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue'; $1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'; }
pid_of() { python3 "$GI" pid; }   # this game's pid, nothing when it is down, non-zero when the list could not be read
gone() { local p; p=$(pid_of) && [ -z "$p" ]; }
port_in_log() { [ -f "$LOG" ] && grep -a -o '\[RimBridge\].*on port *[0-9]*' "$LOG" | tail -1 | grep -o '[0-9]*$'; }

status() {
    local pid; pid=$(pid_of) || return 2
    if [ -n "$pid" ]; then
        local info; info=$(ps_q "\$p=Get-Process -Id $pid; '{0} session={1} started={2:yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss} age_s={3}' -f \$p.Id,\$p.SessionId,\$p.StartTime,[int]((Get-Date)-\$p.StartTime).TotalSeconds")
        local args; args=$(ps_q "(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ProcessId=$pid').CommandLine")
        echo "running pid=$info"
        echo "  cmdline: $args"
        echo "  bridge port in Player.log: $(port_in_log || echo none)"
        return 0
    fi
    echo "stopped"
    return 3
}

steam_pid() { ps_q "(Get-Process steam -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1).Id"; }
# Steam normally runs from the autologon (Run Steam when my computer starts). If it is not
# running, start it: with a remembered login it signs in by itself. The Steam install is
# taken as the folder above RM_STEAMAPPS; if steam.exe is not there, the registry's SteamExe.
steam_up() {
    [ -n "$(steam_pid)" ] && return 0
    local exe="$STEAM_EXE_WIN"
    [ -f "$(dirname "$RM_STEAMAPPS")/steam.exe" ] || exe=$(ps_q "(Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\\Software\\Valve\\Steam').SteamExe")
    [ -n "$exe" ] || { echo "REFUSED: Steam is not running and steam.exe was not found"; return 2; }
    echo "Steam not running: starting $exe -silent"
    ps_q "Start-Process -FilePath '$exe' -ArgumentList '-silent'"
    for _ in $(seq 24); do sleep 5; [ -n "$(steam_pid)" ] && { sleep 20; echo "Steam up (pid $(steam_pid))"; return 0; }; done
    echo "FAILED: Steam did not start within 120 s"; return 2
}

up() {
    local pid; pid=$(pid_of) || { echo "REFUSED: the game list could not be read; not starting a game on a guess"; return 2; }
    if [ -n "$pid" ]; then echo "already running (pid $pid)"; status; return 0; fi
    steam_up || return 2
    if [ -n "$NAMED" ]; then python3 "$GI" launch ${1:+"$1"}; return $?; fi
    local t0; t0=$(date +%s)
    ps_q "Start-Process -FilePath '$EXE_WIN' -WorkingDirectory '$DIR_WIN'"
    sleep 5
    pid=$(pid_of)
    [ -n "$pid" ] || { echo "FAILED: no RimWorldWin64 process 5 s after Start-Process"; return 1; }
    echo "started pid $pid"
    [ "${1:-}" = --wait ] || return 0
    while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 600 ]; do
        if [ -f "$LOG" ] && [ "$(stat -c %Y "$LOG")" -ge "$t0" ] && port_in_log >/dev/null; then
            echo "bridge up on port $(port_in_log) after $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) s"; return 0
        fi
        [ -n "$(pid_of)" ] || { echo "FAILED: game exited during load; tail of Player.log:"; tail -n 15 "$LOG"; return 1; }
        sleep 5
    done
    echo "TIMEOUT: no bridge port in a fresh Player.log after 600 s"; return 1
}

# A fresh or reset save-data folder lacks two files that modcheck run refuses without
# (found on the first remote run, 2026-10-25):
#  - JawaBench/companion_profile.json: with none the companion reports profile 'campaign'
#    and ensure_test_profile raises. Every save in this folder is the runner's (the game is
#    ours, owner 2026-10-25), so 'test' is true; the expiry is renewed to 30 days ahead on
#    every init.
#  - Config/Prefs.xml with runInBackground True: game_focus.preflight refuses
#    (FocusRefused, runInBackground UNREADABLE) without it. The game writes Prefs.xml on a
#    clean exit only, and rewrites it from memory then, so it can be seeded only while the
#    game is stopped. Prefs.template.xml is Archmagi's Prefs minus the screen size.
init() {
    if [ -n "$NAMED" ]; then python3 "$GI" prepare; return $?; fi
    mkdir -p "$RM_GAME_USERDATA/JawaBench" "$RM_GAME_USERDATA/Config"
    local exp; exp=$(date -u -d '+30 days' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    local esc; esc=$(printf '%s' "$DATA_WIN" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g')   # JSON-escape the backslashes
    cat > "$RM_GAME_USERDATA/JawaBench/companion_profile.json" <<EOF
{
  "profile": "test",
  "expiresUtc": "$exp",
  "campaignSaves": "",
  "why": "SteveDesktop test centre: the game and every save in $esc are the runner's (rw_game.sh init)"
}
EOF
    echo "companion profile: test until $exp"
    local prefs="$RM_GAME_USERDATA/Config/Prefs.xml"
    if grep -q '<runInBackground>True</runInBackground>' "$prefs" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Prefs.xml: runInBackground True"; return 0
    fi
    [ -z "$(pid_of)" ] || { echo "REFUSED: Prefs.xml lacks runInBackground True and the game is running (it would overwrite the fix on exit); run down, then init"; return 2; }
    [ -f "$prefs" ] && cp "$prefs" "$prefs.pre-init" && echo "Prefs.xml: old copy kept as Prefs.xml.pre-init"

<ModMetaData>
  <name>RimMandrake: Huge Things</name>
  <packageId>mandrake.rm.hugethings</packageId>
  <author>mandrake</author>
  <supportedVersions>
    <li>1.6</li>

  <description>Huge plants and huge animals that behave like their size. Mass has consequences.

The engine gives every plant and every pawn one cell, however big it is drawn. A
mushroom twenty cells across can only be clicked on the cell it grows from,
pawns walk straight through its stem, and walls get built inside it. A beast
the size of a house walks through a doorway, hides behind a sandbag and gets
penned like a chicken.

Huge Things fixes that for anything that opts in:

- A huge PLANT gets a solid trunk. The cells where its art touches the ground
  are solid (measured per species, and grown into as the plant grows), so pawns
  walk around it and nothing can be built inside it. You still walk under its
  cap. Clicking anywhere on its picture selects it. Trunks give partial cover,
  and shots into them hurt the plant.
- A huge ANIMAL gets a selection hitbox the size of its drawn body.
- A TITAN (any creature of body size 4 or more, or one a mod opts in) gets a
  size tier. Heavy, colossal and titanic creatures crush crates and plants,
  breach walls, hole thin roofs and leave rubble as they walk, struggle under
  overhead mountain, butcher for a curved yield, and the largest leave a corpse
  that becomes a harvest site worked over days.
- The biggest titans smash through giant plants, damaging them as they push
  past; smaller titans go around the trunks like walls.

With Large Pawns (neku.largepawns) loaded, titans also occupy 2x2 to 4x4
cells, using this mod's tiers; without it they stay one cell and everything
else still works.

Mod Settings: one master switch for giant plants and one for giant animals,
each with every detailed behaviour and its tuning beneath. All off is vanilla.

This is the engine only. A plant opts in with the RM_HugePlantExtension, a
race with the RM_HugePawnExtension or RM_TitanicExtension modExtension (or
simply a large enough body size). This mod replaces "RimMandrake: Titanic
Creatures" (mandrake.rm.titaniccreatures), which is now part of it.</description>

    """(path, state, seconds, detail), recording evidence for an eligible test (PASS writes a record,
    anything else deletes it)."""
    ev = _EVID
    rel = _rel(path)
    skip_ev = ev is None or not rel or path not in ev["eligible"]
    cov = _cov_clone(path)          # coverage trace: only where close evidence can count (an isolated checkout)
    kn = _KNOWN if rel and not cov else None
    if skip_ev and not cov and not kn:
        return _run_one(path, cap, est)
    seq = next(_SEQ)
    tdir = Path(os.environ.get("RM_SELFTEST_CACHE_DIR") or STATE_DIR) / "trace" / f"{os.getpid()}-{seq}"
    import suite_evidence as E
    began = time.time()
    try:
        if kn:
            import known_results as K
            env = K.arm_env(tdir, kn["shim"])
        else:
            env = (ev["store"] if ev else E.Store(REPO_ROOT, STATE_DIR)).trace_env(tdir)
        r = _run_one(path, cap, est, env=env)
        if kn:
            _known_record(kn, rel, r, tdir, began)
        elif cov and _KNOWN and rel:
            _known_false_hit(_KNOWN, rel, r)    # traced runs record nothing there, but a contradiction still counts
        if cov:
            _note_covers(path, cov, tdir)
        if not skip_ev:
            if r[1] == "PASS":
                ok, why = ev["store"].record(rel, tdir, r[2])
                (ev["recorded"] if ok else ev["unrecorded"]).append((rel, why))
            else:
                ev["store"].forget(rel)
        return r
    finally:
        E.clear_trace(tdir)


def _own_tmp(env) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    """(env, dir): a TMPDIR of the test's own. Selftests mkdtemp at import and never remove it: 65,000 dirs stood under
    ~/.seat-tmp on 2026-11-01. "" = could not make one; the test still runs, in the shared TMPDIR."""
    try:
        tdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="selftest_run_")
    except OSError:
        return env, ""
    if env is not None and env.get("RM_SELFTEST_ARM"):
        (Path(json.loads(env["RM_SELFTEST_ARM"])["trace"]) / "own_tmp").write_text(tdir)    # exempt from the manifest
    return dict(env if env is not None else os.environ, TMPDIR=tdir), tdir


def _drop_tmp(tdir: str) -> None:
    if not tdir:
        return
    shutil.rmtree(tdir, ignore_errors=True)
    if os.path.lexists(tdir):               # a test that chmods its fixtures read-only
        subprocess.run(["chmod", "-R", "u+rwx", tdir], capture_output=True)
        shutil.rmtree(tdir, ignore_errors=True)


# WSL interop can drop the launch of a Windows exe under load ("UtilAcceptVsock: accept4 failed 110"), and the test reads
# that as its own failure: nothing was measured. Such a red alone runs again, whole; only a real PASS turns it green, and
# the summary counts them so a rising rate stays visible (NIGHTLY_COP_FIX_RED_HMGHDI_RQAA).
INTEROP_DROP, INTEROP_RERUNS, INTEROP_WAIT_S = "UtilAcceptVsock", 2, 15
_INTEROP_RERUN: dict = {}


def _run_one(path: Path, cap: int = 0, est: int = 0, env=None) -> tuple[Path, str, float, str]:
    """(path, state, seconds, detail). detail's first line is the reason for any non-PASS."""
    for attempt in range(INTEROP_RERUNS + 1):
        use, tdir = _own_tmp(env)
        try:
            r = _run_one_in(path, cap, est, use)
        finally:
            _drop_tmp(tdir)
        if r[1] == "PASS" or INTEROP_DROP not in r[3] or attempt == INTEROP_RERUNS:
            return r
        _INTEROP_RERUN[_rel(path)] = attempt + 1
        time.sleep(INTEROP_WAIT_S)


def _run_one_in(path: Path, cap: int = 0, est: int = 0, env=None) -> tuple[Path, str, float, str]:
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        proc, rep = _run_capped(path, per_test_timeout(path), cap, est, env)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        out = proc.stdout + proc.stderr
        tail = out.strip().splitlines()[-40:]
        if _HARNESS:
            if not rep:
                return path, "CRASH", elapsed, ("harness error: contained run gave no wrapper report (rc "
                                                f"{proc.returncode}): {proc.stderr.strip()[-400:]}")
            if not rep.get("ok"):
                return path, "CRASH", elapsed, (f"harness refused to run it: landed in {rep.get('placement')}, "
                                                f"not {HARNESS_SLICE}")
            if rep.get("peak"):
                _PEAK_SEEN[_rel(path)] = rep["peak"]
        state, why = classify(proc.returncode, out, rep if _HARNESS else None, cap)
        if state == "PASS":
            return path, "PASS", elapsed, ("" if out.strip() else "silent: printed nothing at all")
        shown = tail[-20 if state == "CRASH" else -40:]
        # A FAIL above the tail is the only record of what failed; after the tail, so known_reds' first error is unmoved.
        cut = out.strip().splitlines()[:-len(shown)]
        lost = [ln.strip()[:600] for ln in cut if ln.lstrip().startswith("FAIL")][:10]
        return path, state, elapsed, "\n".join([why] + shown + lost)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        return path, "CRASH", elapsed, f"timeout: exceeded {per_test_timeout(path)}s"
    except Exception as exc:  # harness-side failure: OSError, ENOMEM, bad interpreter
        # Never let this escape into as_completed — one raised future would abort the
        # whole loop and print NO summary at all, which is the truncation this file
        # exists to prevent. Report it as a named non-PASS instead.
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        return path, "CRASH", elapsed, f"harness error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"

# Diagnosis of the three nonpass attempts

There is **no production policy defect** in these attempts. The two selftest crashes are a harness/test-output fault. The build failure is a compile error in the new probe. The selftest never reached a verdict, so the L0 policy result is still unmeasured. It is not red and not green.

## 1–2. Selftest CRASH (`UnicodeDecodeError 0xec`): HARNESS fault, almost certainly from the test program's own output

**Likely cause:** the bytes come from `JuvenileTier.dll`'s stdout, not from the dotnet CLI.

- `Row(..., "malformed factor "+bad)` converts `float.PositiveInfinity` and `NegativeInfinity` to strings using the current culture. On .NET 8 with ICU, that produces `∞` and `-∞`.
- When stdout is redirected on Windows, Console encodes with the OEM code page. In cp437, `∞` is exactly byte **0xEC**. The byte after it is `\r` or ` `, which is not a UTF-8 continuation byte, and that matches the error text.
- The offset fits. About 10 `Row` lines precede the first ∞ row, on top of the staging/restore build chatter. The ~109-byte difference between attempts is consistent with different build-output preamble.
- This also explains why attempt 2's fix did nothing. `DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE` and `MSBUILDLOGCODEPAGE` affect only CLI/MSBuild text, not a user program's `Console.WriteLine`. Also, variables set in WSL are not forwarded to Windows `.exe` children unless they are listed in `WSLENV`, so they probably never reached dotnet.exe at all.
- The JuvenileTier.csproj does not compile `JuvenileTierValidationHooks.cs`, so the L0 build was unaffected by failure 3 and the program actually ran. Rows print only after their checks pass, so the rows printed before the crash had passed. Nothing after the first ∞ row is known.

**Bounded repairs (test-local only; no shared `winbuild.py` or runner edit):**

a) In `Program.cs`, make the output deterministic ASCII. This is a fix at the source.
```csharp
using System.Globalization;
static int Main() {
    CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentCulture = CultureInfo.InvariantCulture;
    ...
```
Invariant culture renders `Infinity`, `-Infinity` and `NaN`. It also fixes `"custom "+string.Join(",",ladder)` under comma-decimal locales.

b) **Yes, the wrapper can capture raw streams before rendering**, as long as it bypasses `run_interop`'s decode path for the run step only. The build step can stay on `winbuild.stage_build`, whose output is ASCII here. In `selftest_hugethings_juvenile_tier.py`:
```python
import hashlib, subprocess
def run_raw(cmd, cwd, raw_dir):
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)  # bytes, no decode
    for name, data in (("stdout", p.stdout), ("stderr", p.stderr)):
        path = os.path.join(raw_dir, f"juvenile_tier.{name}.bin")
        with open(path, "wb") as f: f.write(data)
        safe = data.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace").encode("ascii", "backslashreplace").decode("ascii")
        sys.stdout.write(safe)
        print(f"\n[{name}] bytes={len(data)} sha256={hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()} raw={path}")
        if any(b > 0x7F for b in data):
            print(f"[{name}] NON-ASCII at offset {next(i for i,b in enumerate(data) if b>0x7F)}"); return 3
    return p.returncode
```
- Write the raw files outside `src/`, for example under `record['stage']`, which already serves as a Linux-side cwd.
- Propagate the child exit code verbatim.
- The non-ASCII fail-closed rule tightens the bar rather than weakening it, because after repair (a) our own program must emit ASCII.
- Before copying this, check how `run_interop` maps `cwd`. If it isn't a plain Linux path, use the same mapping. The DLL path is absolute, so cwd is immaterial to the program anyway.

## 3. Build FAIL CS1061: probe compile defect in the production assembly, not a policy defect

`JuvenileTierValidationHooks.cs:30` calls `pawn.CurLifeStage`, but `Pawn` has no such member. Your `engine.il.txt` shows that `CurLifeStage` lives on `Pawn_AgeTracker`, and that `Pawn.get_BodySize` uses `ageTracker.CurLifeStage.bodySizeFactor`. The fix is:
```csharp
factor = F(pawn.ageTracker.CurLifeStage.bodySizeFactor);
```
The rest of the stage-selection path checks out against the IL:
- `cachedLifeStageIndex` exists as an Int32.
- Setting it to a value ≥0 skips `RecalculateLifeStageIndex`.
- `GetLifeStageAge` reads only `pawn.def.race.lifeStageAges`, and the probe guards that path.

## Test-oracle faults and risks found

1. **Real fault: `Log.Errors==1` is an absolute count.** If production logs on invalid custom ladders (`{4,8,8}`, `NaN`, `∞`, …) or on any earlier path, the "missing shipped fallback" check fails spuriously. Record `int e0=Log.Errors;` before clearing the cache, then assert `==e0+1` on both reads.
2. **Proof-output risk in the hook:** `thresholds=` prints `TitanicTierUtility.Thresholds`. If that returns only the cached shipped def, the L1 custom-threshold proof would print `4,8,20` while custom settings are in effect. Also emit `TierThresholdsCustomActive` and the three settings values, or the effective ladder that production actually uses.
3. **`Census()` passes stageIndex −1**, so `GetTier` is always "unsupported". That is fine as a census, but the STATEMENT's "actual GetTier" proof needs explicit `Observe(def, i)` calls for each stage of representative defs.
4. **Policy assertions that must be cited to the spec.** These are not faults, but L0 encodes them as truth:
   - Malformed factors (0, −1, NaN, ±∞) and null entries or defs make spacing fall back to the adult tier, even when a valid max of 0.5 exists.

5. **Minor:** the force-loop `DefQualifies` oracle hardcodes 4 instead of the T1 threshold. That is correct at the defaults where it runs, but brittle.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded, offline reefback source measurement. No game, dump, network or build.

Inputs are explicit: repository, installed game directory, selected engine IL receipt,
and optionally a Core archive. Only two exact Core XML members are read from tar;
no archive is extracted. The small inheritance resolver handles the selected XML
shapes only (scalar overwrite, named children, li append, Inherit=False replacement).
It is not a general RimWorld loader or a measurement of a running pawn.
"""
import argparse
import copy
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import tarfile
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

SEA = 'src/RimMandrake/TerminalBiomes/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_SeaBeasts_Invented.xml'
MIASMA = 'src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Defs/BiomeDefs/RM_Miasma.xml'
GREY = 'src/RimMandrake/TerminalBiomes/Defs/BiomeDefs/RM_GreySea.xml'
MOTHER = 'src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_WardenMother.xml'
HT = 'src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/'
CORE = ('Defs/Misc/LifeStageDefs/LifeStages.xml',
        'Defs/ThingDefs_Races/Races_Animal_Base.xml')
SKIP = {'FlowWorks', 'GSS', 'GravShipSystems', 'obj', 'bin', 'art_source'}
TOKENS = ('Reefback', 'AnimalBaby', 'AnimalJuvenile', 'AnimalAdult',
          'AnimalThingBase', 'AnimalKindBase', 'BasePawn', 'baseBodySize',
          'bodySizeFactor', 'lifeStageAges', 'forceEnabled', 'RM_TitanicTier',
          'ageGenerationCurve', 'lifeExpectancy', 'minGenerationAge', 'maxGenerationAge')


def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def f32(v):
    return struct.unpack('<f', struct.pack('<f', v))[0]


def merge(parent, child):
    """Selected shapes, following XmlInheritance. Never sort a stage list."""
    result = copy.deepcopy(parent)
    # RecursiveNodeCopyOverwriteElements removes parent attributes and copies
    # child attributes except Inherit. Name/Abstract must not leak into a child.
    result.attrib = {k:v for k,v in child.attrib.items() if k != 'Inherit'}
    if child.get('Inherit', '').lower() == 'false':
        result[:] = copy.deepcopy(list(child))
        result.text = child.text
    elif not len(child):
        result[:] = []
        result.text = child.text
    else:
        for node in child:
            existing = result.find(node.tag)
            if node.tag == 'li' or existing is None:
                result.append(copy.deepcopy(node))
            else:
                result[list(result).index(existing)] = merge(existing, node)
    return result


def tier(size, floors):
    return next((n for n in (3, 2, 1) if size >= floors[n-1]), 0)


def event_eligible(adult_tier, opted_out, sea_creature, sea_map, has_list, on_list, homed_here, season_ok, t3_on_map):
    """Source-model evaluation of the selected RM_TitanicKernel predicate."""
    if opted_out or adult_tier < 2 or sea_creature != sea_map or not season_ok:
        return False
    if not (on_list if has_list else homed_here):
        return False
    return not (adult_tier == 3 and t3_on_map)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument('--repo-root', type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4])
    ap.add_argument('--game-dir', type=Path, required=True, help='Linux path to installed RimWorld')
    ap.add_argument('--engine-il', type=Path, required=True, help='read_engine.ps1 selected IL output')
    ap.add_argument('--core-archive', type=Path)
    ap.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    repo, out = a.repo_root.resolve(), a.out.resolve()
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    snapshots = out / 'snapshots'
    snapshots.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    manifest = []
    (snapshots/'engine-selected.il.txt').write_bytes(il)
    for fragment in (b'METHOD Verse.Pawn::get_BodySize', b'Single bodySizeFactor',
                     b'Single baseBodySize', b'RecursiveNodeCopyOverwriteElements', b'"Inherit"',
                     b'"false"', b'RemoveChild', b'AppendChild', b'CalculateInitialGrowth'):
        if fragment not in il:
            raise ValueError('incomplete engine input: ' + repr(fragment))
    for rel in ('Version.txt', 'RimWorldWin64_Data/Managed/Assembly-CSharp.dll'):
        p = a.game_dir / rel
        record(str(p), p.read_bytes())
    ladder = HT+'Defs/TitanicTierDefs/RM_TitanicTierDef.xml'
    data = read(ladder)
    record(ladder+':selected node', data, list(ET.fromstring(data)))
    t = ET.fromstring(data)[0]
    floors = [float(t.findtext(f't{i}MinBodySize')) for i in (1, 2, 3)]

    results = {}
    for species in ('RM_ReefbackJuv', 'RM_Reefback', 'RM_WardenMother'):
        race = resolve(definitions[('ThingDef', species)])
        kind = resolve(definitions[('PawnKindDef', species)])
        stages = list(race.find('race/lifeStageAges'))
        base = float(race.findtext('race/baseBodySize'))
        rows = []
        for i, stage in enumerate(stages):
            name = stage.findtext('def')
            factor_text = definitions[('LifeStageDef', name)].findtext('bodySizeFactor')
            # AnimalAdult omits this; the constructor IL explicitly sets 1.
            factor = float(factor_text) if factor_text is not None else 1.0
            size = f32(f32(base)*f32(factor))
            rows.append({'stage': name, 'minAge_years_xml': float(stage.findtext('minAge')),
                         'factor': factor, 'factor_source':
                             ('Miasma RM_WardenMother.xml' if name == 'RM_WardenMotherElder' else 'Core XML')
                             if factor_text else 'LifeStageDef constructor IL default',
                         'body_size_decimal': base*factor, 'body_size_float32': size,
                         'default_GetTier': tier(size, floors),
                         'kind_drawSize': kind.findtext(f'lifeStages/li[{i+1}]/bodyGraphicData/drawSize')})
        results[species] = {'baseBodySize': base, 'stages': rows,
                            'lifeExpectancy': float(race.findtext('race/lifeExpectancy')),
                            'ageGenerationCurve_xml': race.findtext('race/ageGenerationCurve'),

    biome_rows = {}
    for rel, defname, animal in ((MIASMA,'RM_Miasma','RM_ReefbackJuv'), (GREY,'RM_GreySea','RM_Reefback')):
